component.name: Dialog
component.description: A titled panel that takes focus: modal over an inert page, or non-modal in the page flow. Focus returns to its trigger on close.

useWhen: Asking the user to confirm an action before it happens, especially a destructive one.
A short task the user must finish or cancel before returning to the page, such as editing one record.
Showing details of a selected item next to the content it came from, without leaving the page (nonModal).

notFor.case: Showing the result of an action, such as a saved confirmation
notFor.because: Taking focus to report a result interrupts the user for something they don't need to act on.
notFor.note: Use Alert (Phase 5e, ADR-031) once it ships.

notFor.case: Choosing one of a few actions on an item
notFor.because: A list of actions is a menu: it opens from its trigger and closes on select.

notFor.case: Revealing more detail inside a list of sections
notFor.because: Detail that belongs to its section reads best in place.

patterns.name: confirm-action
patterns.useWhen: Confirming an action: title, consequence, Cancel and a confirm button; Cancel gets data-autofocus when the action is destructive.

patterns.name: edit-form
patterns.useWhen: Editing a few fields of one record without leaving the page: fields in Body, Cancel and Save in actions.

patterns.name: detail-panel
patterns.useWhen: A non-modal panel beside the content it describes, opened from a selected item and showing that item's details.

donts.case: Putting React's autoFocus on a child to choose the first focused element
donts.because: React focuses it at mount, before the dialog opens, so the call is lost and Dialog focuses its title instead.
donts.instead: Put data-autofocus on the child Dialog should focus when it opens.

donts.case: Opening a modal Dialog from inside another modal Dialog
donts.because: Stacked modals leave users unsure which one Escape closes and where focus returns.
donts.instead: Replace the open dialog's content, or close it before opening the next one.

donts.case: Putting a DropdownMenu inside a Dialog
donts.because: DropdownMenu closes on Escape without preventing its default, so one Escape closes the menu and the dialog together.
donts.instead: Keep DropdownMenu out of Dialog until it calls preventDefault on Escape; only then add it to accepts.

donts.case: Placing the dialog's main buttons in children
donts.because: Actions keeps them in the footer, right-aligned and visible while Body scrolls.

donts.case: Body text in the default text colour, or at a size other than body-default
donts.because: Dialog body text reads slightly muted under the title, at the system's standard reading size.
donts.instead: Use Text color="subtle" at its default size for paragraphs in children.

donts.case: More than one accent Button in actions
donts.because: The accent button marks the one action the dialog exists for (ADR-024).
donts.instead: Use one accent (or danger) Button for the confirm action and neutral for the rest.
